reason: Hair-fringed = ciliate: a margin fringed with hairs. Floras' 'ciliate' already goes to PATO:0001408 (see config/flora_union_pairs.tsv).
Sub- + fimbriate: the named value with value_qualifier 'sub' (pattern 01, approximate value), as for 'suborbicular'.
A compound of two values, trigonous (FLOPO:0991120) and globose (spherical, PATO:0001499); both terms exist.
'Uni-/bi-/multicostate' is a count of ribs; 'costate → rib' is already in config/flora_counted_parts.tsv, so it needs only the 'uni-' = 1 numeral.
Glochidate = glochidiate, bearing barbed bristles, which is already a synonym of FLOPO barbed. 'With glochids' could also be read as glochid (FLOPO_0986043) present on cactus fruits.
Half-globose = half of a sphere: PATO:0005000 hemispheroid.

The colour backbone (config/botanical_colour_synonyms.tsv) maps 'rust'/'rusty'/'ferruginous' to orange FLOPO:0988002. PATO:0070059 rusty is a texture (oxidised iron), not a colour, so it must not be used.
Sub- + villous: the named value with value_qualifier 'sub' (pattern 01).

target: new: position of the widest part
reason: The examples say 'widest below/at/above the middle': the position of the widest part along the length of the blade. No PATO term covers this, and it is not a whole outline such as ovate. It belongs in one pattern with 'widest above the middle'.
Atro- + castaneous = dark chestnut. The colour table maps 'dark chestnut' and 'castaneous' to PATO:0001287 red brown (NARROW).
A compound of oblong (PATO:0000946) and spathulate (spatulate, PATO:0001937) with a degree word. Both values exist.
Embedded = immersed, which the previous review mapped to sunken (C329). A stylopodium 'not embedded' is one not sunk into the disc.
'Set with scales' = bearing scales on the surface: PATO:0001804 scaly. The covering is named in the phrase itself, unlike the rejected 'covered'.
Sub- + capitate, with value_qualifier 'sub'. On an inflorescence it is the head-like cluster; on a stigma it is the rounded head shape, as in the existing split between the two FLOPO classes.
Same as rule C236 for 'inequilateral': unequal-sided leaves and fruits are asymmetrical.

target: new: position of the widest part
reason: Position of the widest part along the length of the blade; no PATO term (an obovate outline would say more than this). Same pattern as 'widest below'.
Birostrate = two-beaked: a count of beaks on a beaked (FLOPO:0991028) fruit. It needs a 'rostrate → beak' row in config/flora_counted_parts.tsv.
The 'cage' is corolla lobes joined at their tips (as in Ceropegia): like parts fused, with the apex region (slot 1). Too few statements for a new shape term.
A carrion smell is an offensive, foul odour: FLOPO foetid (synonym foul-smelling).
A count of ovules ('ovulate → ovule' is already in the counted-parts table). 'Many' is a non-numeric count, which the pattern keeps as measurement_value_not_numeric.
A compound of oblong (PATO:0000946) and falcate (falciform, PATO:0002215) with a degree word. Both values exist.

label: twice compound
definition: A structural quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being compound, with its primary divisions themselves compound. NOTE: FLOPO:0991014 bipinnate is the pinnate case only. This also covers biternate leaves and inflorescences whose branches are branched again. PATO has no compound-leaf quality.
reason: Leaves and inflorescences 'twice compound' do not say whether the division is pinnate, ternate or palmate, so bipinnate would claim too much.
Seeds without endosperm (exalbuminous): complement of has_part some endosperm.
'Tinged' is a faint wash of the colour: bronze with value_qualifier 'approximately' (pattern 01, as for 'greenish').
A loose likeness used for different things (flattened pinnately branched branch systems, female scales). It has no single quality and too few statements.

label: involucre-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's similarity to the appearance of an involucre: a set of bracts crowded in a whorl round the base of a flower or inflorescence. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991200 bract-like and PATO:0002457 leaf-like, worded as they are.
reason: A real botanical comparison, in the same family as bract-like and spike-like. Only 3 statements back it.
A vague impression of vigorous growth, not a defined quality of a part.
Lunate = crescent-shaped (rule C314). 'Obliquely' only adds that the crescent is lopsided.
Partly below ground: subterranean with value_qualifier 'approximately'. Too few statements for a new class like half-inferior.
'Unpleasant smell' is already a synonym of FLOPO foetid.
